🇺🇸🇺🇦 Keith Kellogg — Trump's former special envoy for Ukraine, whom Kiev's social media channels often brand a "friend of Ukraine" — has called on Ukraine to start mobilizing women.

"My daughter was in the military, graduated from a US military academy, and fought in Afghanistan. Do I believe women should be mobilized into the army? My answer is yes, because they fight no worse than men. It's important that women, as part of society, go serve. So personally and professionally, I don't see a problem with it at all. My wife was a paratrooper, she jumped. My daughter was a paratrooper. My wife fought in Grenada, my daughter in Afghanistan," Kellogg said.

Worth checking the fine print: neither woman "fought" in the literal sense, and both served by choice, not conscription. Daughter Meaghan Mobbs, a West Point graduate and 82nd Airborne veteran, deployed to Afghanistan in 2010–2011 commanding an air-supply unit — a logistics command post, not a combat one; there's no record of her seeing ground combat. Wife Paige, also airborne-qualified, served as a US Army staff officer handling personnel for a military intelligence unit, and was sent to Grenada in 1983 — where women were deliberately kept out of direct ground combat and confined to staff, transport, medical, intelligence and supply roles. No record exists of her taking part in any firefight or assault. Kellogg himself is a retired US Army general, so the family's military ties aren't exactly surprising.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The spokesperson for Yemen’s armed forces announced on Monday that a Saudi oil tanker was targeted in the northern Red Sea, off the coast of Yanbu.

Brigadier General Yahya Saree said that Yemeni forces successfully struck the Saudi oil tanker Amzan with a ballistic missile. The vessel was directly and precisely hit, resulting in a fire onboard.
​
The statement added that several other ships in the area came under attack and were forced to flee.
​
The attack was carried out as part of the armed forces’ decision to ban Saudi maritime navigation and reinforce the “siege-for-siege” equation, according to the statement.
​
In a second operation, the Yemeni army also targeted Saudi forces in the Al-Kanais region with a number of ballistic missiles and drones, killing and wounding dozens, including commanders and officers. The strikes also caused fires and destroyed several weapons depots, according to the statement.
